evidence.quote: Today the Federal Open Market Committee kept interest rates near zero and maintained our asset purchases.
We’re clearly a ways away from considering raising interest rates. It’s not something that, that is on our radar screen right now.
Participants expect that the economy will continue to move toward our standard of “substantial further progress.”
This is not moderately above 2 percent. This is well above 2 percent.
I would say, in the near term, that the, the, the risks to inflation are probably to the upside.
I think we’re, we’re some way away from, from having had substantial further progress with, with max—toward the maximum-employment goal.

parsed.rationale: Policy stays highly accommodative with rate hikes off the radar, but the Chair begins deliberating on taper timing and composition, acknowledges inflation well above 2 percent with upside risks, and stresses readiness to respond. On net these offset, leaving a near-neutral to slightly hawkish signal.
